questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose to study in NYC because of its vibrant energy and dynamic atmosphere. Having previously visited the city, I was eager to experience living there. Additionally, I was drawn to New York University due to its strong reputation for academic excellence and its welcoming, supportive community.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: NYU is a large institution with extensive experience hosting exchange students, making it easy to access the information I needed and get in touch with their staff. Additionally, KU provided detailed guides, ensuring I had no trouble obtaining the necessary information from their end as well.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had some questions regarding housing at NYU and I received an answer to these via email.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: As a law student, you can choose to live in either D’Agostino Hall or Hayden Hall, both really close to the teaching facilities. That said, it’s not common for exchange students to be offered on-campus housing. I’m not sure why I got the chance, but I’d definitely recommend others to give it a shot if they can!

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Meal plan was offered and all rooms have cooking facilities as well. I did not choose the meal plan as it was rather expensive and I wanted to discover the local cuisine.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Living on campus might seem pricey at first, but compared to the area, it’s actually not. It was super convenient being so close to the teaching facilities, and overall, I was really happy to have the chance to live on campus. The rooms were not in any way luxurious and some people also had problems with stains on the carpet from previous residents (which the university then took care of though).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They have a bidding system that you have to get used to but it is actually not that difficult. You can see how much students had to offer previous years to get the course. This made sure you had an idea how popular the courses were, and thus how much you should offer on the courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There were video guides as well as written guides. Furthermore, you can ask for assistance at the office of graduate affairs if need be.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted. I had to bid a lot of points for one of the courses that I wanted but I also ended up getting it.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Spend some time on the bidding system to make sure you understand how it works. Some courses have room for everyone and do therefore not require for you to bid any points.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: None of the courses I took were particularly easy, unlike what some exchange students might experience in other destinations. That said, I didn’t find the courses overly challenging either, and I was able to achieve good grades without too much effort.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Cold calling is allowed and some professors like to cold call a lot. I had to get used to this, but I felt that the professors were kind when asking the questions, and I could also see some benefits from the cold calling. Apart from that, I would not say that the style of teaching was vastly different from the one at UCPH although students generally participate a little more in the classes at NYU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to U.S. Law (mandatory introduction course)
Antitrust law
Contracts for LLM students
Negotiating corporate transactions.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Negotiating corporate transactions might have been one of the best courses I have ever taken. I felt like I developed my skills on a professional level as well as on a personal level. It was fun to practice mock cases each time.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Health insurance was quite expensive even compared to the U.S. Moreover, New York in general is quite expensive

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I did not have to spend much money in books as these were provided by the university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are tons of options when it comes to activities at NYU. I was part of the run club and the European Law society. Moreover I joined a lot of other events that were provided for free.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The boat ride in the fall as well as the fall ball and the trips to broadway were great fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed visiting Washington D.C. on an extended weekend trip. I also went to Cancun, Mexico which was great fun too and not too pricey

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I lived on campus, and while the area around Washington Square Park is lively and vibrant, it is also quite noisy and busy, which took some time to get used to. Aside from that, I found it easy to adapt to New York, as it is such an inclusive city with people from all over the world.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Spend time with the LLM's. They are also international and thus new to the city and to the language just like you. They are super friendly and are eager to make new friends too.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Many of the JD students focus heavily on their studies and have little time or interest in socializing. While I enjoyed spending time with the other exchange students and the LLMs, it would have been nice to spend more time with the American students as well.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: New Yorkers and Americans tend to be friendlier and more talkative than Danes. I really appreciated this, as it made it easier to start new conversations and meet new people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy all of it and take some classes that you find interesting. Spend time eating out and go for long walks in the city.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I transferred credits for the Introduction Course, reducing my semester workload to 10 credits instead of the usual 12. This gave me greater flexibility and more time to concentrate on the courses I was taking.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know the city by heart and to have that feeling of a second home. In the beginning everything is new and exciting, but I enjoyed the last couple of months particularly much, because by then I had established routines and a social network allowing myself to relax and enjoy it a bit more.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding a balance between studying and socializing was important to me. I wanted to focus on my studies, but I also wanted to have time to explore the city and spend time with others.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
